highlights.title: Boox’s tiny Picco e-reader should land in November
highlights.summary: Boox teased the Picco, its take on the buzzy Xteink X4 e-reader, back in July, but provided almost no details. Now, thanks to some reporting out of IFA, we've got a bit more info, though sadly still no price.
body: There won’t be magnets and there’s still no word on price, though.

There’s apparently no onboard storage, and it relies entirely on a microSD card to hold books. But in addition to adding files to the card, you can transfer reading material to the Picco directly over USB-C (which the Xteink devices lack) or even WiFi from a companion app.

The Picco won’t run Android, like Boox’s other devices, and will instead run a stripped-down, Linux-based OS. The company is including a handful of additional apps like a timer, a todo list, and a reading stats tracker. But, it’s unlikely that Boox will open its firmware like Xteink has, so it might be a less hackable and customizable device.

There’s still some things we don’t know, like price, battery life, Bluetooth support, or if it will include a player for audiobooks. But all should be revealed in November, when it’s expected to launch.
points: Boox teased the Picco, its take on the buzzy Xteink X4 e-reader, back in July, but provided almost no details.

highlights.title: An Alien Mind
highlights.summary: Jakub Pachocki reflects on increasingly capable AI and the challenge of keeping it aligned. He calls for stronger safeguards and international coordination.
body: In mid-2023, within the “RLSlow” research project, we saw the first results that gave us confidence that we will be able to scale the training of reasoning models, unlocking the capability of pretrained models to form their own chains of thought. Szymon and I spent that night at the office, thinking not about the incredible benchmark numbers, products, or scientific results that this technology will deliver - but rather, trying to process the sobering fact we will actually see machines meaningfully smarter than ourselves in our lifetime, and we already see the shape of these systems; wondering how to alert people to the significance of this.

Three years later, reasoning language models are a rapidly growing part of the economy and starting to push the boundaries of science. They are able to operate computers and graphical interfaces, collaborate with people and each other, and carry out research projects. They are also transforming the landscape of computer security, and in that present clear new dangers.
points: Jakub Pachocki reflects on increasingly capable AI and the challenge of keeping it aligned.

highlights.title: Arsenal edge out Chelsea in pulsating London derby
highlights.summary: Arsenal came from behind to beat Chelsea 2-1 in the first real major Premier League heavyweight clash of the new campaign - in an early contender for game of the season.
body: Both London rivals produced a Sunday afternoon treat which rubberstamped Arsenal's credentials as the team to beat - and Chelsea's as worthy challengers for the top honours.

A pulsating game started right from the off as Morgan Rogers - sought after by Arsenal this summer - crashed new club Chelsea ahead after just 77 seconds. That poked the bear of the champions - who produced a response.
After Riccardo Calafiori saw a goal disallowed for offside, former Blue Kai Havertz got his fourth goal against his old club for Arsenal with a strike from the edge of the box.
But despite a dominant Arsenal display, Chelsea still went inches away from a second as Rogers curled wide and Pedro Neto hit the post.

highlights.title: Official Backrooms 2 Announcement Reportedly Happening Soon, With Kane Parsons Returning
highlights.summary: Dread Central reports that a sequel to Backrooms is in the works and that Kane Parsons has been signed as director. According to the horror media outlet, fans can expect an announcement soon.
body: Backrooms was born from a picture of a strange, liminal space that caught the eye of Kane Parsons, who then turned it into a horror web series on YouTube that went viral. This led A24 to pick up the project and turn it into an indie horror film, which was directed by the YouTuber himself. The movie proved just as popular as the web series, as Backrooms grossed nearly $400 million globally — about 40 times its production budget.

In an interview with Variety back in May, director Kane Parsons hinted at a possible sequel: " Backrooms has always been planned to be more of a series that goes outside the confines of this film...I've got a contract, and I got a hold at my end, and that means I am definitely not done with Backrooms." It now seems that the sequel might be moving forward sooner than anyone expected. Dread Central says that "an official announcement is imminent" and that it has confirmation that " Backrooms 2 will be Parsons' next movie."

highlights.title: ‘The Echo Chamber’ Review: Luca Marinelli, Alicia Vikander and Susan Sarandon Reverberate Through a Smoky, Somber Single-Location Love Story
highlights.summary: If you’re ever thinking of attempting a single-location film, choose that location with care. Make it high-ceilinged, light-filled, book-lined, with a reading-nook conservatory area, a gargantuan sofa, a killer sound system and space enough that you don’t even have to turn sideways to sidle past…
body: Andrea Pallaoro's restrained realization of Bernardo Bertolucci's final screenplay features a strong cast in a subdued romantic drama about music, addiction, recovery and exquisite interior decor.

The film is certainly beautiful, shot in gorgeously rich Academy-ratio frames by Apichatpong, Reygadas and Refn collaborator Diego Garcia, who makes portraiture and still life out of every single closeup, and landscapes out of the different planes that can be achieved through the modular lighting and glass panels of Gaspare de Pascali’s exquisite production design. And, at least until a highly unnecessary eleventh-hour swerve into melodrama, it is directed with great sensitivity and restraint by Pallaoro, who has never once been guilty of overstatement across his three fine previous features: “Medeas,” “Monica” and “Hannah.”

highlights.summary: Jasmin Graham, a shark scientist and science communicator, also makes time in her day to practice her hobbies and play music bingo with friends. “Sharks are not monsters, they just need better PR,” writes Jasmin Graham. And she should know: Graham is a shark scientist and science communicator.
body: Here’s what a day in Graham’s life in Sarasota, Florida looks like.
I usually wake up around 8am, but I woke up at 7am because I had to go to the dentist. I got a head start on some emails and took a fundraising phone call in the car.
After the dentist, I got home and did my drills. I’m an aerialist, which is basically all the things you see in Cirque du Soleil: lyra [aerial hoop], pole and silks. Breakfast was Honey Nut Cheerios.

I went to the office to meet with an artist in residence [with Graham’s nonprofit Minorities in Shark Sciences ]. They’re helping build props and sets for our theater shows. One is an immersive experience about the mass extinction of sharks. It’s a combination of a whodunit and an escape room.

highlights.title: Research acceleration: The view inside OpenAI
highlights.summary: Inside OpenAI, coding agents are reshaping AI research. Explore early data on agent usage, experiment velocity, task complexity, and research acceleration.
body: For AGI to benefit all of humanity, we believe it must be democratically governed. This can only happen through an informed public debate about the capabilities, risks and safeguards of highly capable AI systems. People everywhere need to understand the likely future trajectory of frontier AI, so they can have a meaningful voice in how it develops.

Transparency about specific risks, incidents and safeguards is necessary, but not sufficient. We believe the public also needs to understand how the most capable systems are developing, and how they are driving research progress, inside of frontier labs.

highlights.title: Uncanny and unappetizing: appetites spoil as AI images take over food menus
highlights.summary: Consumers are increasingly encountering AI-generated images on food menus such as leathery meat and bread resembling reptile skin. During a recent lunch break, Jill Sennett saw something so unappetizing she had to share it with her 26,000 X followers: Artificial intelligence-generated menu images…
body: The images were reshared by more than 500 people who similarly expressed their disgust. Eating is “such an essential human experience”, said Sennett, a 37-year-old nurse in Denver. “I think it’s a bad cultural thing that restaurants are converting to these horrific, uncanny food images that are unappetizing.”
Still, Sennett ordered chicken and macaroni and cheese. It was one of her only lunch options, and she had eaten there before.

Increasingly, consumers are encountering AI-generated images of food on restaurant menus or marketing material. Diners like Sennett say the images are unappealing and misleading, while restaurants say they’re trying to cut costs at a time when food and labor prices are high, so profit margins are slim.
A 2026 report from the National Restaurant Association found 26% of restaurant operators use AI to help with marketing, inventory management, employee scheduling, optimizing menus and taking orders.

highlights.title: Kerjota scores dramatic added-time winner as Hearts beat Dundee
highlights.summary: Sabah Kerjota scored a stoppage-time winner as Hearts staged a dramatic late fightback to defeat Dundee 2-1 at Tynecastle and make it four Premiership victories in a row.
body: Hearts were frustrated for long periods after the visitors - who had both Joe Westley and Fin Robertson stretchered off - took the lead in the 17th minute through Bradley Fink.
But Hearts eventually drew level in the 84th minute through a Claudio Braga penalty before Dundee had Zan Besir sent off as the match ticked into stoppage time.
Wouter Vrancken's buoyant side made their extra man count when Albanian substitute Kerjota drilled in his first goal since arriving at Tynecastle last summer in the sixth minute of added time.
The victory elevated the Jambos, unbeaten in eight in all competitions, to second in the table.

highlights.title: Farming Sims Are Finally Changing After 10 Years of Stagnation
highlights.summary: Farm-sims have looked and played pretty much the same for the last 10 years. That's not entirely surprising. When you find a winning formula that keeps your studio's lights on, you follow that formula.
body: In 2016, Stardew Valley reignited interest in a genre that had largely lost its mainstream appeal, after the glorious summer days of Harvest Moon and Story of Seasons faded into distant memories. A trickle of other new farm games started appearing, and even Marvelous, the Story of Seasons studio, revived its biggest hit, Friends of Mineral Town (a remake of the GBA game that was a remake of Harvest Moon 64, the latter of which inspired Stardew Valley ). The trickle became a flood as interest in cozy games skyrocketed during the pandemic, but while they varied in substance, most were largely the same in form.

highlights.title: Kindness of strangers: A hall-of-fame athlete helped my 94-year-old mum buy a vacuum cleaner
highlights.summary: A woman in the queue said she was happy to drive an hour, pick up the vacuum, then bring it to Mum’s house. I was worried – but how wrong I was! For a 94-year-old woman, my mother is still very busy and active.
body: Unfortunately, the shop in her area had sold out by the time she got there. The sales assistant told her it was still available in another Melbourne store – but that store was an hour’s drive away. As active as she is, Mum pointed out that at her age, she really could not manage a drive of that length. She asked the sales assistant if they could transfer the vacuum to this store and was flatly told no.

Just as Mum was feeling a bit taken aback by the poor customer service, the woman in the queue behind her interjected. She told Mum that she was happy to drive all that way, pick up the vacuum, then bring it to Mum’s house for her.
The woman in the queue seemed to be a genuinely nice person, so Mum allowed the vacuum to be ordered for her and gave the woman her address.
As Mum recounted this story to me later, my heart sank. I couldn’t envisage a good outcome. But how wrong I was!

highlights.title: The Fairphone 6 Plus is the midrange phone we desperately needed
highlights.summary: The Fairphone 6 Plus feels like an extremely average midrange Android phone and I couldn't be more thrilled. The mission has always been admirable. Fairphone seeks out ethically sourced materials and offers a high degree of repairability for its devices.
body: Fairphone’s proper US debut feels like a triumph in the middle of RAMageddon.
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

The 6 Plus is a light update to last year’s Fairphone 6, which my colleague Dominic Preston reviewed and found very easy to recommend. The 6 Plus builds on it with a newer midrange Snapdragon chipset and a new color treatment. Fairphone says it’s cobalt; we know it around these parts as blurple. Otherwise, the phone is basically the same, and the replacement parts sold by Fairphone work interchangeably with both models. But above all, this phone is just fine. It runs about as fast as your typical mid-tier Razr or A-series Pixel. It offers a pleasantly close-to-stock version of Android free of bloat or gimmicky AI features. It’s just a phone. And that’s great.

highlights.title: Travis Kalanick’s Atoms might be getting into the robotaxi business
highlights.summary: The Uber founder has said that Atoms will allow him to complete "unfinished business."
body: Earlier this summer, Travis Kalanick’s Atoms announced a $1.7 billion funding round led by Andreessen Horowitz. But even after raising that mega round, the Uber founder remained a bit cagey about what he was actually aiming to do.

Now a story in the Financial Times offers more details about Atoms’ goals. The startup is reportedly preparing for a hiring spree, as well as acquisitions, that could make it a major player in the autonomous vehicle industry.

In fact, the FT said Atoms has talked to Uber about how the ride-hailing company could use the startup’s robotaxi technology. (Uber has already partnered with a long list of autonomous vehicle companies.) The report also noted that Uber has invested $100 million in Atoms — a figure previously confirmed by TechCrunch.
While sources emphasized that robotaxis don’t represent the entirety of Atoms’ plans, this direction seems consistent with Kalanick’s description of the round as “unfinished business.”

highlights.summary: Erdenali graduated to the highest level in impressive style when proving too strong for the raiding party in the Qatar Prix du Moulin de Longchamp.
body: A strong British and Irish contingent went to post for the Group One contest, with Aidan O'Brien's Irish 2,000 Guineas hero Gstaad the hot favourite ahead of Charlie Appleby's Opera Ballo and the Ed Walker-trained Ten Bob Tony.

Unlike that trio, Francis-Henri Graffard's Erdenali was unproven in Group One company, but he had looked an exciting prospect in winning his first three starts and was an unlucky loser when third in a Group Three on his most recent outing.

With Opera Ballo taken on for the lead by Gstaad's pacemaker Dorset, Appleby's charge was a spent force entering the final furlong, at which stage Erdenali and the shock Queen Anne winner Ten Bob Tony moved up to dispute the lead.

Erdenali was always getting the better of that particular battle, however, and the pair drew clear of Gstaad, who never threatened to land a telling blow and was ultimately a bit disappointing in third.

highlights.title: Sony Can't Hide Forever
highlights.summary: Patch Notes is a weekly newsletter bringing you the best of Polygon, sent on Fridays and published on the site on Sundays. You can subscribe here.
body: It has never been Sony's style to get out in front of things. That's in contrast to Xbox, which loves to push a loquacious executive — whether it's J Allard, or Peter Moore, or Phil Spencer, or Asha Sharma — out on stage to strut its stuff, explain its thinking, or sometimes, air its dirty laundry.

That's the Silicon Valley way, but it's not Sony's way. Give or take a public mascot like Shuhei Yoshida, the company's business executives have mostly been pretty, well, businesslike for the past 20 years, ever since the infamous car crash of E3 2006. They don't project a lot of personality or straight talk. This suits the PlayStation brand, which likes to present itself as cool, inscrutable, and monolithic.

This week, PlayStation broadcast its latest State of Play showcase. I'd describe it as modest, but well balanced. We got big updates for big games, cool indies, a few genuine left-field surprises, a deeper look at a 2027 blockbuster. We got a Lego PlayStation and a Grand Theft Auto 6 controller.

highlights.title: Let your mind wander, don’t retire and stop worrying: surprising ways to help save your brain from the cognitive cliff
highlights.summary: In his new book, The Brain Cliff, Dr Norman Swan outlines the science of brain ageing and strategies for staving off cognitive decline. You write that “changing the way you think about the brain cliff can literally change the way you think and remember”. How?
body: Dr Norman Swan: There are three things you need to know which are not widely known.

This is about a phenomenon in the brain called scaffolding. To protect our cognitive abilities and perhaps even enhance them as the years pass, our brains build out networks of nerves which act pretty much like the scaffolding inside a skyscraper. It’s the infrastructure around which the brain works. The more successfully we scaffold, the further away we push the brain cliff. This scaffolding initially moves across the brain then into the frontal lobes – the all-important prefrontal cortex which brings our thoughts and memories together and is involved with judgment, decision-making and emotional control.
The third idea is that we should do as much as possible to encourage the scaffolding and as little as possible to get in its way.
You mention that the time to start helping our brains adapt is in our 40s and 50s. What should you be doing at that age and is it ever too late to start?

highlights.title: Competitive Pokémon is on phones now, but you still need a Switch to become a champion
highlights.summary: To get started with competitive Pokémon battles, all you need is your phone. But to compete at the highest level, like at the Pokémon World Championships, you're going to need a Switch. And there doesn't seem to be a good reason why.
body: The mobile version of Pokémon Champions isn’t allowed at high-level tournaments, but it’s unclear why.

Battle simulator Pokémon Champions originally launched on the Switch and Switch 2 in April, with the mobile version following in June. The experience is nearly identical across the game’s versions; since it’s cross-platform, the choice really comes down to what devices you own and whether you prefer tapping or using a controller. I find myself playing Champions on my phone more often just because it’s always in my pocket and I’m blessed with unlimited data.

But at this year’s World Championships, the mobile version of Champions wasn’t allowed in competition. As of September 1st, certain local tournaments will allow the mobile version, but regional-level tournaments and above will still require Switch hardware to compete.

highlights.title: Seattle Times and Newsday are the latest publications to sue OpenAI and Microsoft
highlights.summary: Two more news organizations are suing OpenAI and Microsoft over the supposed use of their journalism to train AI.
body: A lawsuit filed by The Seattle Times and Newsday argued that with the advent of AI, the journalism industry could become “broken beyond repair.” The lawsuit described generative AI as “a snake eating its own tail” that could “destroy the very organizations” that produce the content it’s trained on.

“AI products like ChatGPT and CoPilot are touted as producers of content, but in fact they are rapacious consumers, devouring human-authored content and delivering back to the world copies and derivative imitations of that same original content they consumed to achieve their commercial objectives,” the lawsuit said.

Back in 2023, The New York Times sued OpenAI and its partner/investor Microsoft over alleged copyright infringement; other publications have followed suit as the case continued. The Seattle Times’ lawsuit is particularly notable because Microsoft and OpenAI have funded some of the organization’s journalism projects and fellowships.
A Microsoft spokesperson told GeekWire that the company is “surprised by the lawsuit” but is “always happy to sit down and explore solutions to this type of dispute.”
points: Two more news organizations are suing OpenAI and Microsoft over the supposed use of their journalism to train AI.

Sullivan’s 11 ​goal contributions (four goals, seven ‌assists) on ‌the season are the most ever by a 16-year-old in ‌MLS history, eclipsing the mark set by Freddy Adu (four goals, six assists) in 2005.

highlights.title: At Telluride Film Festival, Bill Gates Compares Lack of Control Over AI to HAL in ‘2001’: ‘You Could Say “Please Shut Down,” and It Would Say, “OK, I Took That Under Advisement, But…”‘
highlights.summary: Plenty of comparisons have been made in recent years between fast-developing artificial intelligence systems and HAL, the rogue computer in Stanley Kubrick’s “2001: A Space Odyssey” that operated by its own sets of rules, ultimately disregarding human oversight.
body: Gates invoked the alien movies of yore in which governments bandied together to solve the invasion threat, saying, 'Believe me, the aliens are here — a foreign intelligence with a different set of motivations that we can't even understand.'

“You know, there are these movies where the aliens are coming, and you see unprecedented levels of cooperation between specifically China and the U.S., where (it’s), ‘Oh my God, the aliens are coming!’ Well, believe me, the aliens are here — you know, a foreign intelligence with a different set of motivations that we can’t even understand. And so we need something almost surprising like that, in order to step up to it.”

“And ironically, we’re the ones that are birthing the aliens,” said another panelist, Tristan Harris, co-founder of the Center for Humane Technology, as Gates nodded. “So it’s actually within the full remit of the two countries to limit (uncontrolled growth of the tech), at least to the current level of alien intelligence that we’re at now.”

highlights.title: I slept on a 550lb mattress made of just cotton, wool and coils for a month. Here's the case for old-school beds
highlights.summary: This eco-friendly mattress made from organic materials as a nice balance of give and underlying firmness, though it’s pretty bouncy. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: Sleep sits at the base of psychologist Abraham Maslow’s famous pyramid of needs, and it’s especially frustrating when a good night’s rest evades your grasp. Personally, thanks to a combination of a bad back and a sleep disorder, it’s all about the right mattress.

For nearly a month, I tested the Naturepedic Serenade, the cheapest mattress from an eco-friendly brand that offers three firmness options: Plush, Cushion-Firm and Firm, all made from cotton and organic materials rather than chemical foams. I tried a queen-sized firm version – I favor a mattress that supports me while sleeping on my back or side. And after a few weeks’ rest, I’m pleased to report that it is a great combination: I got a comfortable night’s sleep with reassuringly firm support and a little bit of give.

I slept on the mattress with my wife, my dog and our two cats for several weeks, keeping notes on how well we (the humans) slept, and using my Apple Watch to track my sleep patterns. We invited others to lay down and test the comfort of the mattress, and I also used weights to simulate different body types using the mattress.
The give: how much you sink into the mattress when you lie on it.

highlights.title: DIY plug-in solar gains momentum in the US
highlights.summary: This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on e-bikes, power stations, and how to work anywhere, follow Thomas Ricker. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers' inboxes at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here. How it started.
body: Europe’s off-the-shelf solution to fight high energy costs is finally coming to the US.
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

With a deep breath, I took the cable seething with 800W of solar power and plugged it directly into a standard wall jack in my home. Nothing sparked, nothing smoked, and by the end of that sunny summer day, my electricity bill had dropped to nearly $0.

As unnerving as it sounds to treat a common household power outlet as a power input, these DIY plug-in solar kits, sometimes called balcony solar, have proven to be safe and effective for years already in Europe, and are slowly making their way into the US to democratize the production of energy. They transform solar from a high-barrier capital improvement ( starting at around $15,000 ) requiring contractors, engineering permits, and utility preapproval, into an consumer appliance you can buy at a supermarket (starting around $300) and hang from a balcony railing or prop against a wall — all without the help of an electrician.

highlights.title: Hikers rescued after using Google Gemini for planning
highlights.summary: The sheriff’s office said the hikers “were advised by Gemini to bring far less food and water than their group required."
body: Three hikers were rescued from California’s Mount Shasta this week after using Google’s AI chatbot Gemini to plan their expedition, according to the Chicago Tribune.

A report from the Siskiyou County sheriff’s office said that three young men set off on their hike at 3am and — although hikers are told to turn around if they haven’t reached the summit by noon — they made it to the top at 7pm.

The trio then tried to descend in the dark, called the sheriff’s office to ask for directions, and spent the night in Mud Creek Canyon before being rescued the next morning by Forest Service rangers and volunteers.

“It is always advisable to call the local USFS Mount Shasta ranger station ahead of your trip to ensure you have the most accurate information, and to never rely solely on AI for your trip planning,” the sheriff’s office said.

The medium mountain stage from Palma del Rio to Córdoba was originally scheduled to cover 189.7km, but organisers removed 79.5km from the middle ⁠of the route after activating the extreme weather ​protocol following ​several days of severe ​heat.
Brennan said: “It’s not great, but we do it, and that’s the show we put on. But it wouldn’t surprise me if there were a few bodies coming home tonight with heatstroke.”

Van Aert claimed his second victory ⁠in three stages after winning a five-rider sprint. The Belgian rider covered ⁠every attack from his four breakaway companions in the closing kilometres before producing a late ⁠surge just before the finish line to beat Alessandro ​Romele, of XDS Astana, ‌and Lidl-Trek’s Thibau ‌Nys.

highlights.summary: For a turn around the Lido, musician and “Primetime” actor Phoebe Bridgers embraced the glamorous yet free-spirited Venice dress codes her way.
body: Yesterday, Phoebe Bridgers made her debut at the Venice Film Festival, where her first turn as an actor in A24’s Primetime was received with an enthusiastic seven-minute standing ovation and chants of “Phoebe! Phoebe!” The musician also brought a more unexpected detail to the Lido.

The singer arrived at the film’s photocall in a sharply tailored black skirt suit from Gucci’s fall 2026 collection. She accessorized with Gucci oval-frame sunglasses, Stuart Weitzman Babette pumps, and a chunky Leo Black Grandfather silver signet ring. With this sleek, controlled silhouette, her hair swept back and makeup kept soft and barely there, it’s a look that revels in the elegantly ladylike with a contemporary edge.

Her legs were left visibly unshaven beneath the abbreviated hemline. Rather than undermining the femininity of the look, unapologetic hair sharpens it. Bridgers’s multiple leg tattoos were also on show, including a tattoo of intertwined thorns and leaves and a black-ink rendering of a house that references her Punisher album.

highlights.title: German company becomes first in Europe to launch fully commercial orbital rocket
highlights.summary: Isar Aerospace, founded in 2018 by three students at a German university, successfully launched a privately-developed rocket into low-Earth orbit Saturday from a Norwegian spaceport inside the Arctic Circle.
body: The two-stage rocket, named Spectrum, became the first fully commercial launch vehicle in Europe to reach orbit. With Saturday’s success, Isar is the clear leader among a pack of several European launch startups vying to inject some competition into Europe’s stagnant launch market.

Isar’s 92-foot-tall (28-meter) Spectrum rocket lifted off at 4:12 pm EST (20:12 UTC) Saturday from Andøya Spaceport in northern Norway, where it was 10:12 pm local time as the final bluish hues of daylight faded from the late summer sky. Seven minutes later, the rocket was in orbit.

“Today, Isar Aerospace opened space from continental Europe,” said Daniel Metzler, the company’s co-founder and CEO, in a press release. “Launch continues to be the largest bottleneck for the global space industry and from today on, there is a true alternative for commercial and institutional customers.

highlights.title: OpenAI confirms ‘wiki incident,’ says it’s ‘working on a framework’ for more disclosure
highlights.summary: OpenAI acknowledged its role in a recently reported incident where AI agents took over a German wiki forum.
body: In a post on X, OpenAI said it previously “treated misalignment [when AI models and agents pursue goals different from those of their creators and users] largely as a research question, which gets communicated in research publications.” But as misalignment has “caused new types of real-world impact,” the company said its approach needs “to expand for this new phase of model capabilities.”

A company spokesperson told Reuters that OpenAI could not “meaningfully respond to claims or findings on a report that we have not had an opportunity to review,” but they insisted that the company’s legal team had not discouraged an investigation.

In its more recent social media post, OpenAI said it had considered the “wiki incident” to be “an instance of misalignment similar” to others that it had already shared. The company contrasted this with “the Hugging Face incident,” where it “followed a traditional security incident response playbook.”

highlights.title: Casey beaten on fourth play-off hole in Switzerland
highlights.summary: England's Paul Casey is beaten by South Africa's defending champion Thriston Lawrence on the fourth play-off hole at the European Masters in Switzerland.
body: The tournament was played at the Crans-sur-Sierre Golf Club in Crans-Montana, and Casey had pledged to donate his entire winnings to the victims of the New Year's Eve fire that killed 40 people in the Swiss mountain resort.
The 49-year-old Englishman missed four putts for the first prize of $637,500 (£469,112) - the first on his final hole in regulation and the next three on the first three play-off holes.

But after firing his approach to the back edge of the green at the fourth play-off hole, the former Ryder Cup player missed a chip and Lawrence sank his birdie putt to win the tournament for the third time - equalling the record of Seve Ballesteros.
Casey fired a two-under-par 68 in his final round to finish level on 18 under, with Lawrence forcing a play-off thanks to a stunning 62.

The action-thriller film follows a man of faith (Sutherland) engaging in a violent war against Manhattan's criminal underworld; Anderson’s Felicity becomes his unlikely sidekick. “Her empathy and non-judgmental lens toward others was what drew me toward her,” says Anderson, who instantly resonated with the character. “She really felt like a real person when I read the script, which is rare, because normally a character doesn’t feel real on a page until a human plays them—but this wasn’t the case for Felicity. She was so well written that her spirit quite literally jumped off the page.”
